URL: https://news.sky.com/story/labour-members-call-on-government-to-cancel-palantirs-nhs-contract-13591968
Sky News EXCLUSIVE — Saturday 26 September 2026 02:31 BST. By Amanda Akass, political correspondent.

HEADLINE: Labour members call on government to cancel Palantir's NHS contract
Sub: A conference committee will decide on Saturday whether the emergency motion will be debated and voted on.

FACTS:
- Delegates at the Labour party conference in Liverpool are trying to pressure the government into cancelling its £330m NHS contract with US tech giant Palantir.
- An emergency motion has been submitted calling on the Department of Health and Social Care to exercise a break clause in its contract with Palantir to run the Federated Data Platform (FDP).
- The FDP uses Palantir's AI-powered data analytics software to bring together information from across the health service so hospitals can analyse it more easily.
- The motion was put forward by the Labour-affiliated Socialist Health Association and at least three constituency parties. It claims Palantir is "facing numerous allegations of involvement in serious breaches of human rights, including due to it developing technology for Israel's military to use in its unlawful occupation of Palestinian land and genocide in Gaza". (Israel denies allegations of genocide in Gaza.)
- The motion's authors also highlight the recent appointment of Labour peer and former deputy leader Tom Watson as senior vice president at Palantir UK, arguing "links between senior politicians and private companies creates distrust amongst voters, particularly where public contracts are awarded... the Labour government has a responsibility to uphold public trust in politics".
- A CONFERENCE COMMITTEE WILL DECIDE ON SATURDAY 26 SEPTEMBER whether the emergency motion will be debated and voted on during the conference, which starts on Sunday.
- The motion is backed by Labour's left-wing faction Momentum and the Palestine Solidarity Campaign; authors hope Unison will support it.
- Both the science and technology and health and social care select committees have called for the government to invoke the February 2027 termination clause of the FDP contract, which was signed in 2023, as have the British Medical Association and the union Unison.

QUOTE (Lord Tom Watson, announcing his Palantir appointment on X last week): "Palantir is the most interesting company on the planet, doing work of real consequence: helping Britain and its allies defend themselves, helping police protect our citizens and helping NHS staff get patients treated and home sooner."

QUOTE (Rathi Guhadasan, chair of the Socialist Health Association): "Palantir's human rights record is easily enough to disqualify it from government contracts - from its use in Donald Trump's immigration crackdown, to Israel's use of its technology to target Palestinians in its genocide in Gaza."

QUOTE (Rathi Guhadasan): "But even on its own terms, a growing body of evidence within the NHS shows its technology is not fit for purpose or cost effective. Andy Burnham should show he means change, listen to NHS workers, and cancel Palantir's NHS contract."

QUOTE (Department of Health and Social Care): "The benefits of the FDP service are clear, with thousands more patients benefitting every month, including through the reduction in the number of unnecessary days spent in hospital after treatment."

- Ministers told MPs earlier this week the Palantir contract would be "reviewed in line with standard contract management processes and the outcome will be announced in the normal way in due course".
- Palantir had not responded to a request for comment; it previously said it was appointed to run the FDP "in line with public contract regulations" and claimed "Palantir software is helping to deliver better patient care", including more than 100,000 additional operations and a reduction in discharge delays.
